q: Ayat-ul-Kursi is found in which Surah?
e: It is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah, in the third Para.

q: The longest verse of the Quran (Ayat-ud-Dayn, about writing down debts) is in which Surah?
e: Verse 282 of Al-Baqarah is the longest verse.

q: How many Surahs of the Quran are named after prophets?
e: Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim, Muhammad and Nuh.

q: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran?
e: Twenty-five prophets are named in the Quran.

q: Which prophet's name is mentioned most often in the Quran?
e: ). Hazrat Musa is named about 136 times.

q: How many times is the name "Muhammad" mentioned in the Quran?
e: The name Muhammad occurs four times and Ahmad once (Surah As-Saff).

q: Who is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran?
e: Maryam is named, and the 19th Surah bears her name.

q: Who is the only Companion mentioned by name in the Quran?
e: Zaid is named in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:37).

q: The Huroof-e-Muqatta'at (disjointed letters) appear at the start of how many Surahs?
e: Twenty-nine Surahs open with letters such as Alif-Lam-Mim.

q: During whose caliphate was the Quran first compiled into one volume?
e: After many Huffaz were martyred at Yamama, Abu Bakr ordered the compilation on Umar's advice.

q: Who headed the work of compiling the Quran under Hazrat Abu Bakr?
e: Zaid bin Thabit, a chief scribe of revelation, did this work.

q: Which Caliph is called "Jami-ul-Quran" for sending standard copies to the provinces?
e: Usman united the Ummah on one standard script and reading.

q: The Quran was revealed over a period of about:
e: Roughly 13 years in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.

q: Surah Al-Isra is also known as:
e: The 17th Surah is called both Al-Isra and Bani Israel.

q: Which Surah is described in the Quran itself as "Ahsan-ul-Qasas" (the best of stories)?
e: The phrase occurs at the start of Surah Yusuf.

q: The story of the People of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf) and Zulqarnain is told in which Surah?
e: Surah Al-Kahf is the 18th Surah.

q: The rules for distributing spoils of war are given in which Surah?
e: Al-Anfal 8:41 lays down the fifth (Khums).

q: The eight categories of people entitled to Zakat are listed in which Surah?
e: At-Tawbah 9:60 lists the eight heads of Zakat.

q: The detailed shares of inheritance are laid down in which Surah?
e: An-Nisa verses 11, 12 and 176 fix the heirs' shares.

q: The command of fasting in Ramadan is given in which Surah?
e: Al-Baqarah 2:183–185 made fasting obligatory in 2 AH.

q: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah is called a "clear victory" (Fath-e-Mubeen) in which Surah?
e: Surah Al-Fath was revealed on the return from Hudaybiyyah.

q: Which battle is called "Yawm-ul-Furqan" (Day of Distinction) in the Quran?
e: The term is used for Badr in Surah Al-Anfal.

q: The incident of Abraha's army of elephants is described in which Surah?
e: Surah Al-Fil recalls the destruction of the army in the Year of the Elephant.

q: Which Surah is named after a metal?
e: Al-Hadid means iron.

q: Which bird carried Hazrat Sulaiman's letter to the Queen of Saba, according to Surah An-Naml?
e: ). The Hud-hud brought news of the Queen of Saba.

q: In which Surah does every verse contain the word "Allah"?
e: Every verse of the 58th Surah contains the name Allah.

q: In the Hanafi school, how many places of Sajdah-e-Tilawat are there in the Quran?
e: Hanafis count 14; Shafi'is count 15 with a second Sajdah in Surah Al-Hajj.

q: Who made the first Persian translation of the Quran in the Subcontinent?
e: Shah Waliullah's Persian translation is called Fath-ur-Rahman.

q: Who made the first literal Urdu translation of the Quran?
e: Shah Rafiuddin made the literal one and his brother Shah Abdul Qadir the idiomatic one (Muzih-ul-Quran).

q: "Tafhim-ul-Quran" was written by:
e: Maududi's commentary runs to six volumes.

q: The final prohibition of intoxicants appears in which Surah?
e: Al-Maidah 5:90 calls intoxicants and gambling the work of Satan.

q: Which night is described in the Quran as better than a thousand months?
e: Surah Al-Qadr describes the Night of Power.

q: The verse declaring the Holy Prophet (PBUH) "Khatam-un-Nabiyyin" is in which Surah?
e: Al-Ahzab 33:40 declares the finality of prophethood.

q: Which was the last complete Surah to be revealed?
e: An-Nasr is generally held to be the last Surah revealed as a whole.

q: Surah Al-Hujurat mainly deals with:
o: Social manners and ethics of the Muslim community
e: It forbids mockery, suspicion, spying and backbiting and teaches verification of news.

q: Makki Surahs mostly deal with:
e: Makki Surahs build belief; Madani Surahs carry most legal rulings.

q: "Sihah Sitta" refers to:
o: The six authentic books of Hadith
e: They are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

q: Who compiled Sahih Bukhari?
e: Imam Bukhari was born in Bukhara and died in 256 AH.

q: "Al-Muwatta" is the Hadith collection of:
e: Imam Malik of Madinah compiled the Muwatta.

q: "Musnad" is the famous Hadith collection of:
e: The Musnad of Ahmad contains close to thirty thousand narrations.

q: Which Companion narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
e: Abu Hurairah narrated 5,374 Ahadith.

q: Which Umm-ul-Mu'minin narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
e: Hazrat Aisha narrated 2,210 Ahadith.

q: A Hadith whose meaning is from Allah but whose words are of the Prophet (PBUH) is called:
e: A Hadith Qudsi is a sacred Hadith that is not part of the Quran.

q: A Hadith narrated by so many people in every generation that agreement on a lie is impossible is called:
e: Mutawatir is the highest grade in terms of transmission.

q: The chain of narrators of a Hadith is called:
e: Sanad is the chain; Matn is the text.

q: A Hadith traced directly to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is called:
e: Marfu goes back to the Prophet, Mawquf to a Companion, Maqtu to a Tabi'i.

q: A fabricated Hadith is technically called:
e: Mawdu means forged and falsely attributed.

q: "Muttafaq Alaih" means a Hadith found in:
e: The agreement of the two Sahihs is the strongest form of authenticity.

q: The science dealing with the biographies and reliability of narrators is called:
e: Asma-ur-Rijal examines each narrator's life and trustworthiness.

q: Which Umayyad Caliph ordered the official collection of Hadith?
e: He instructed scholars such as Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri to gather Hadith.

q: "Riyadh-us-Saliheen" was compiled by:
e: Imam Nawawi also compiled the well-known Forty Hadith.

q: "Fath-ul-Bari", the famous commentary on Sahih Bukhari, was written by:
e: Ibn Hajar's commentary is the best-known on Bukhari.

q: "Al-Kafi", one of the four main Shia books of Hadith, was compiled by:
e: Kulaini's Al-Kafi is the first of the Kutub-e-Arba'a.

q: The "Sahifa" of Hammam bin Munabbih is important because it is:
o: One of the earliest surviving written collections of Hadith
The first commentary on the Quran
e: Hammam was a student of Abu Hurairah.

q: The collection of Imam Tirmidhi is commonly called:
e: It is known as Jami-ut-Tirmidhi.

q: Sunnah literally means:
e: In Shariah it means the way of the Prophet (PBUH) in word, deed and approval.

q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Year of the Elephant, which corresponds to about:
e: He was born in Makkah in Rabi-ul-Awwal of the Year of the Elephant.

q: What was the name of the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) father?
e: Abdullah died before the Prophet's birth.

q: The Holy Prophet's (PBUH) mother, Hazrat Amina, died at:
e: She died at Abwa on the way back from Madinah when he was six.

q: Who was the foster mother who nursed the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in the desert of Banu Sa'd?
e: Halima of the tribe of Banu Sa'd nursed him.

q: After his grandfather's death, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was brought up by:
e: Abu Talib protected him until his own death in the tenth year of prophethood.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry Hazrat Khadija?
e: He was 25; she was about 40.

q: "Hilf-ul-Fuzul", in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part as a young man, was:
o: A treaty with the Jews of Madinah
A pact to protect the oppressed in Makkah
e: The pact was concluded in the house of Abdullah bin Jud'an.

q: Who was the first woman to accept Islam?
e: Hazrat Khadija believed at once after the first revelation.

q: Who was the first among children to accept Islam?
e: Hazrat Ali accepted Islam at about ten years of age.

q: Who was the first martyr of Islam?
e: Sumayyah, mother of Ammar bin Yasir, was killed by Abu Jahl.

q: The first migration of Muslims to Abyssinia took place in which year of prophethood?
e: A small group migrated in the fifth year (about 615 CE).

q: Who was the king of Abyssinia who gave refuge to the Muslims?
e: Najashi (Negus), named Ashama, protected the emigrants.

q: The social boycott of Banu Hashim in Shi'b Abi Talib lasted about:
e: It lasted from the 7th to the 10th year of prophethood.

q: The tenth year of prophethood is called "Aam-ul-Huzn" (Year of Sorrow) because of the deaths of:
e: Both of his great supporters died in the same year.

q: Who went with the Holy Prophet (PBUH) on the journey to Taif?
e: Zaid bin Harithah was with him at Taif.

q: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the occasion of:
e: The prayers were given during the Night Journey and Ascension.

q: How many people of Madinah took the Second Pledge of Aqabah?
e: Seventy-three men and two women took the pledge in the 13th year of prophethood.

q: In which cave did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr stay during the Hijrah?
e: They stayed three days in the Cave of Thawr.

q: Which was the first mosque built by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
e: He built it at Quba before entering Madinah.

q: In whose house did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stay on reaching Madinah?
e: His she-camel Qaswa knelt near Abu Ayyub's house.

q: The "Mithaq-e-Madinah" was:
o: A peace treaty with the Quraysh
A charter regulating relations among the Muslims, Jews and others of Madinah
e: The Charter of Madinah is often called the first written constitution.

q: The change of Qibla from Bait-ul-Maqdis to the Ka'bah took place in:
e: The command (Al-Baqarah 2:144) came in the second year of Hijrah.

q: The Battle of Badr was fought on:
e: 313 Muslims defeated about 1,000 Quraysh.

q: How many Muslims fought in the Battle of Badr?
e: The commonly reported number is 313.

q: In the Battle of Uhud, who led the Quraysh cavalry that attacked from behind?
e: Khalid, not yet a Muslim, attacked through the pass the archers had left.

q: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was martyred at Uhud?
e: Hamza is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (leader of the martyrs).

q: Who suggested digging a trench in the Battle of Ahzab (5 AH)?
e: Salman suggested the Persian method of a defensive trench.

q: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded in:
e: It was signed in Zil-Qa'dah 6 AH as a ten-year truce.

q: Who represented the Quraysh in finalising the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
e: Suhail bin Amr negotiated and Hazrat Ali wrote the document.

q: The pledge taken under a tree at Hudaybiyyah is called:
e: The Quran (48:18) declares Allah's pleasure with those who pledged.

q: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah is most instructive for diplomacy because it shows that:
o: Force is always better than talks
Treaties should never be made with opponents
Accepting hard terms for peace can bring greater long-term gain
Envoys may be harmed in war
e: The Quran called this outwardly unequal treaty a clear victory; Islam then spread quickly.

q: The fort of Qamus at Khyber was conquered by:
e: Khyber was conquered in 7 AH; Ali defeated Marhab.

q: In which battle did Hazrat Khalid bin Walid receive the title "Saifullah"?
e: After three commanders fell at Mu'tah (8 AH), Khalid saved the army.

q: Makkah was conquered in:
e: The Prophet entered Makkah with 10,000 Companions and declared a general amnesty.

q: The Battle of Hunain was fought against which tribes?
e: It was fought in Shawwal 8 AH, just after the conquest of Makkah.

q: Which was the last Ghazwa led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
e: The Tabuk expedition was in Rajab 9 AH against the Byzantines.

q: The army of Tabuk is known as:
e: It means the army of hardship, raised in great heat and scarcity.

q: In which Hijri year was Hajj made obligatory?
e: Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH; Abu Bakr led the Hajj that year.

q: The Farewell Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) was delivered at:
e: It was delivered on 9 Zil-Hajj, 10 AH.

q: Which of these was a central theme of the Farewell Sermon?
o: Equality of all people and the sanctity of life and property
e: The sermon is seen as a charter of human rights.

q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in:
e: He passed away in Rabi-ul-Awwal 11 AH (632 CE) at the age of 63.

q: Where is the Holy Prophet (PBUH) buried?
o: In the chamber of Hazrat Aisha
e: The chamber is now inside Masjid Nabawi.

q: Which ruler tore up the letter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
e: The Persian emperor tore the letter carried by Abdullah bin Huzafa.

q: Who was the first Muezzin of Islam?
e: Bilal gave the first Azan in Madinah.

q: Who was the mother of the Prophet's (PBUH) son Ibrahim?
e: All his other children were born of Hazrat Khadija.

q: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar?
e: Hafsa bint Umar kept the first compiled copy of the Quran.

q: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was called "Umm-ul-Masakeen" (mother of the poor)?
e: She was known for her generosity to the poor.

q: How many daughters did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have?
e: Zainab, Ruqayya, Umm Kulsoom and Fatima.

q: What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr?
e: His name was Abdullah bin Usman (Abu Quhafa); his title was Siddiq.

q: "Ashra Mubashshara" are the ten Companions who were:
o: Given the good news of Paradise
e: They include the four Caliphs, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Awf, Saad, Saeed and Abu Ubaidah.

q: Which Companion is known as "Amin-ul-Ummah" (trustee of the Ummah)?
e: The Prophet (PBUH) gave him this title.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Which is the first pillar of Islam?
e: ). The five pillars are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: What is the total number of Fard Rak'ats in the five daily prayers?
e: Fajr 2, Zuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3 and Isha 4.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: How many Takbirs are said in the funeral prayer?
e: The Janazah prayer has four Takbirs and no Ruku or Sajdah.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The funeral prayer is:
e: If some Muslims perform it, the duty is lifted from the rest.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: "Salat-ul-Istisqa" is offered for:
e: Istisqa is the prayer for rain in drought.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: "Salat-ul-Kusuf" is offered at the time of:
e: Kusuf is for a solar eclipse and Khusuf for a lunar eclipse.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: What is the rate of Zakat on savings, gold and silver?
e: One-fortieth is due after one lunar year on wealth above the Nisab.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: What is the Nisab of gold for Zakat?
e: 7.5 tolas of gold or 52.5 tolas of silver.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: "Ushr" on rain-fed farm produce is:
e: It is one-tenth on rain-fed land and one-twentieth on artificially irrigated land.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: In which Hijri year was fasting in Ramadan made obligatory?
e: Fasting and Zakat both became obligatory in 2 AH.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Ramadan is which month of the Islamic calendar?
e: It falls between Sha'ban and Shawwal.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The Kaffarah for deliberately breaking a Ramadan fast includes fasting for how many consecutive days?
e: If one cannot fast, sixty poor persons are to be fed.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Staying in the mosque for worship in the last ten days of Ramadan is called:
e: I'tikaf of the last ten days is a Sunnah.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Which act is the most essential pillar (Rukn-e-Azam) of Hajj?
e: The Prophet (PBUH) said: "Hajj is Arafah."

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: On which date do pilgrims stay at Arafat?
e: 9 Zil-Hajj is Yawm-e-Arafah.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The rites of Hajj are performed during:
e: They begin on Yawm-ut-Tarwiyah (8th) and end with the days of Tashriq.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: One circuit round the Ka'bah is called:
e: A Tawaf consists of seven Shawts.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Running between Safa and Marwa is called:
e: Sa'i recalls Hazrat Hajra's search for water.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Where do pilgrims spend the night after leaving Arafat?
e: At Muzdalifah they combine Maghrib and Isha and collect pebbles.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The Hajj in which Umrah and Hajj are performed with a single Ihram is called:
e: Ifrad is Hajj alone; Tamattu is Umrah, then a new Ihram for Hajj.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The Miqat for pilgrims coming from Madinah is:
e: Zul-Hulaifah (Abyar Ali) is the Miqat of the people of Madinah.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The farewell circuit of the Ka'bah before leaving Makkah is called:
e: Tawaf-e-Wida is the last rite before departure.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Which angel is responsible for bringing revelation to the prophets?
e: Jibrail (Ruh-ul-Amin) brought the revelation.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Which angel will blow the trumpet on the Day of Judgement?
e: Israfil will blow the Sur.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The Zabur was revealed to:
e: ). Tawrat to Musa, Zabur to Dawud, Injil to Isa and the Quran to Muhammad (PBUH).

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Which prophet is called "Khalilullah" (friend of Allah)?
e: ). Musa is Kalimullah, Isa is Ruhullah and Ismail is Zabihullah.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Which prophet is called "Abul-Anbiya" (father of the prophets)?
e: ). Many later prophets descended from him through Ishaq and Ismail.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Which prophet is known as "Zun-Nun" (the man of the fish)?
e: ). Yunus was swallowed by a great fish.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: How many Fard acts are there in Wudu according to the Quran (Al-Maidah 5:6)?
e: Washing the face, washing the arms, wiping the head and washing the feet.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Dry ablution with clean earth when water is not available is called:
e: The Quran permits Tayammum in 4:43 and 5:6.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The four sacred months of the Islamic calendar are:
e: Fighting was forbidden in these four months.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Eid-ul-Adha is celebrated on:
e: Eid-ul-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: Belief in the oneness of Allah is called:
e: Tawhid is the foundation of the Islamic creed.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: The life between death and the Day of Resurrection is called:
e: Barzakh means a barrier or interval.

section: Beliefs, worship and pillars of Islam
q: "Sadaqat-ul-Fitr" should be paid:
e: It lets the poor share in the joy of Eid.

q: Where was Hazrat Abu Bakr elected as the first Caliph?
e: The leaders of the Ansar and Muhajirin met at Saqifah Banu Sa'idah.

q: The false prophet Musailimah was killed in which battle?
e: Many Huffaz were martyred at Yamama, which led to the compilation of the Quran.

q: The Caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr lasted about:
e: He was Caliph from 11 AH to 13 AH (632–634 CE).

q: Who first took the title "Amir-ul-Mu'minin"?
e: Abu Bakr was called Khalifat-ur-Rasul; Umar took the title Amir-ul-Mu'minin.

q: Who introduced the Hijri calendar?
e: He introduced it around 17 AH, counting from the year of the Hijrah.

q: The Battle of Qadisiyyah was fought against the:
e: Saad bin Abi Waqqas defeated the Persian general Rustam.

q: The decisive Battle of Yarmouk (636 CE) was fought against the:
e: Yarmouk opened Syria to the Muslims.

q: Who conquered Egypt in the Caliphate of Hazrat Umar?
e: Amr bin al-Aas conquered Egypt and founded Fustat.

q: Hazrat Umar was martyred by:
e: A Persian slave stabbed him during the Fajr prayer in 23 AH.

q: Which Caliph is called "Zun-Nurain" (possessor of two lights)?
e: He married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Ruqayya and Umm Kulsoom.

q: The first Muslim naval fleet was built in the Caliphate of:
e: Muawiya, governor of Syria, raised the fleet and Cyprus was taken.

q: Hazrat Ali shifted the capital from Madinah to:
e: Kufa in Iraq became his capital.

q: The Battle of Jamal (36 AH) was fought near:
e: It is called the Battle of the Camel after the camel of Hazrat Aisha.

q: The Battle of Siffin (37 AH) was fought between Hazrat Ali and:
e: It ended in arbitration (Tahkim).

q: The Kharijites were defeated by Hazrat Ali at:
e: The Battle of Nahrawan was fought in 38 AH.

q: "Nahj-ul-Balagha" is a collection of the sermons, letters and sayings of:
e: Sharif Razi compiled it.

q: Who founded the Umayyad dynasty?
e: Muawiya founded it in 41 AH (661 CE) with Damascus as capital.

q: The tragedy of Karbala took place on:
e: Imam Hussain was martyred in 680 CE during the rule of Yazid.

q: Which Umayyad Caliph is often called the "fifth rightly-guided Caliph"?
e: He ruled from 717 to 720 CE and was known for justice and piety.

q: Spain was conquered in 711 CE by:
e: Tariq defeated King Roderick; Gibraltar (Jabal-ut-Tariq) bears his name.

q: Who founded the city of Baghdad?
e: The second Abbasid Caliph founded Baghdad in 762 CE.

q: The "Bait-ul-Hikmah" (House of Wisdom) of Baghdad flourished most under:
e: Under Mamun it became a great centre of translation and research.

q: Baghdad was sacked by the Mongols under Hulagu Khan in:
e: The last Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad, Al-Musta'sim, was killed.

q: Which dynasty founded Al-Azhar in Cairo?
e: The Fatimids founded Cairo and Al-Azhar in the tenth century.

q: Salahuddin Ayyubi recaptured Jerusalem after the Battle of:
e: ). He defeated the Crusaders at Hattin and then took Jerusalem.

q: The Mongols were stopped by the Mamluks at the Battle of:
e: The Mamluks of Egypt won at Ain Jalut in 1260.

q: Constantinople was conquered in 1453 by:
e: Mehmed II is known as Fatih (the Conqueror).

q: The Ottoman Caliphate was abolished in:
e: The Grand National Assembly of Turkey abolished it on 3 March 1924.

q: Muslim rule in Spain ended with the fall of:
e: Granada surrendered to Ferdinand and Isabella.

q: Which Muslim physician wrote "Al-Qanun fi't-Tibb" (The Canon of Medicine)?
e: The Canon was a standard medical text for centuries.

q: Who is regarded as the father of algebra?
e: The word algebra comes from his book "Al-Jabr wal-Muqabala".

q: "Kitab-ul-Manazir", the famous work on optics, was written by:
e: Ibn al-Haytham is called the father of optics.

q: Who wrote the "Muqaddimah" and is regarded as a founder of sociology?
e: Ibn Khaldun was born in Tunis in 1332.

q: "Ihya Ulum-ud-Din" was written by:
e: Al-Ghazali is known as Hujjat-ul-Islam.

q: Which Muslim scholar first described the pulmonary circulation of blood?
e: Ibn al-Nafis described it in the thirteenth century, long before William Harvey.

q: "Kitab-ul-Hind" was written by:
e: Al-Biruni came to India in the time of Mahmud of Ghazni.

q: "Kashf-ul-Mahjub" was written by:
e: ). It is among the earliest Persian works on Sufism.

q: "Hujjatullah-il-Baligha" was written by:
e: It explains the wisdom behind the rulings of Shariah.

q: Who is known as "Mujaddid Alf Sani"?
e: He opposed Akbar's Din-e-Ilahi and is known for his letters (Maktubat).

q: "The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam" is a collection of lectures by:
e: In it Iqbal calls Ijtihad the principle of movement in Islam.

q: "Islam at the Crossroads" and "The Road to Mecca" were written by:
e: Muhammad Asad was born Leopold Weiss in Austria-Hungary.

q: The Seerah work "Ar-Raheeq-ul-Makhtum" was written by:
e: It won first prize in a Seerah competition of the Muslim World League.

q: The Urdu "Sirat-un-Nabi" was begun by Shibli Nomani and completed by:
e: Nadvi was Shibli's student.

q: The earliest biographer of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), whose work survives in the edition of Ibn Hisham, is:
e: Ibn Hisham edited Ibn Ishaq's Sirat Rasul Allah.

q: What are the four primary sources of Islamic law in Sunni jurisprudence?
e: These four are the agreed sources.

q: The consensus of the jurists of the Ummah on a legal question is called:
e: Ijma is the third source of Islamic law.

q: Extending a known ruling to a new case because of a shared cause (Illat) is called:
e: An example is extending the ban on wine to other intoxicants.

q: The effort of a qualified jurist to derive a ruling from the sources is called:
e: Its opposite, following another jurist's ruling, is Taqlid.

q: Which qualification matters most for responsible Ijtihad?
o: Deep knowledge of the Quran, Sunnah, Arabic and legal principles
e: A Mujtahid must master the sources and methods of law.

q: What was the real name of Imam Abu Hanifa?
e: He was born in Kufa in 80 AH and died in 150 AH.

q: "Kitab-ul-Kharaj", written for Caliph Harun al-Rashid, is the work of:
e: Abu Yusuf, student of Abu Hanifa, was the first Qazi-ul-Quzat (chief justice).

q: "Al-Risala", the first systematic work on the principles of jurisprudence, was written by:
e: It set out the method of Usul-ul-Fiqh.

q: In Islamic law, the science of inheritance is called:
e: Faraid are the fixed shares of the heirs.

q: When a husband compares his wife to the back of his mother, the act is called:
e: Surah Al-Mujadilah condemns Zihar and prescribes an expiation.

q: The dissolution of marriage at the wife's request in return for compensation is called:
e: In Khula the wife usually returns the Mehr.

q: What is the Iddat (waiting period) of a widow who is not pregnant?
e: Al-Baqarah 2:234 fixes it.

q: Punishments fixed by the Quran and Sunnah are called:
e: Ta'zir is discretionary punishment; Qisas is retaliation; Diyat is blood money.

q: Blood money paid to the heirs of a victim is called:
e: Diyat is compensation for killing or injury.

q: The tax taken from non-Muslim citizens in return for protection and exemption from military service was called:
e: Kharaj was the land tax.

q: A partnership in which one party provides the capital and the other provides labour and management is called:
e: Profit is shared in an agreed ratio and financial loss falls on the capital provider.

q: A sale in which the seller discloses the cost and adds an agreed profit is called:
e: Murabaha is cost-plus sale, widely used in Islamic banking.

q: An Islamic lease contract is called:
e: Ijarah transfers the use of an asset for rent.

q: Gain from games of chance and pure speculation is forbidden in Islam under the heading of:
e: Maysir is gambling; Riba is interest; Gharar is excessive uncertainty.

q: Hoarding goods to raise prices is called:
e: Islam forbids hoarding essential goods.

q: The classical institution of "Hisbah" was mainly concerned with:
e: The officer in charge was the Muhtasib.

q: The public treasury of the Islamic state was called:
e: Hazrat Umar organised it as a regular institution.

q: The principle of "Shura" requires a ruler to:
o: Consult competent people before deciding public matters
Decide alone and inform people later
e: The Quran commands consultation in 3:159 and 42:38.

q: Rules on dealings between people, such as trade, contracts and family affairs, are called:
e: Ibadat cover acts of worship; Mu'amalat cover social and financial dealings.

q: In Islamic civilisation the basic unit of society is the:
e: Islam builds society on a stable family.

q: The basic difference between "Deen" and religion in the narrow sense is that Deen:
o: Covers the whole of life: belief, worship, morals, society and state
e: Deen is a complete code of life.

q: Accountability in Islamic governance means that an office-holder:
o: Is answerable to Allah and to the people for a trust
e: Public office is an Amanah (trust).

q: An act that brings reward if done and no sin if left is called:
e: Mustahab (Mandub) is a recommended act.

q: The rights owed to fellow human beings are called:
e: Islam places great weight on Huquq-ul-Ibad.

q: Property dedicated permanently to a religious or charitable purpose is called:
e: In Waqf the asset is kept and its benefit goes to charity.

q: Islamic law allows a bequest (Wasiyyat) to non-heirs up to what share of the estate?
e: The limit of one-third comes from the Hadith of Saad bin Abi Waqqas.

q: In the Quran (49:13), the only basis of superiority among human beings is:
e: ). "The most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you."

q: Which Surah was revealed on the return from the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
e: Surah Al-Fath gave the good news of a clear victory.

q: Which Surah is named after a woman?
e: Surah Maryam is the 19th Surah; An-Nisa means "the women" in general.

q: Surah Al-Fatihah has how many verses?
e: It is called As-Sab'ul-Mathani, the seven oft-repeated verses.

q: The command of Wudu is given in which Surah?
e: Al-Maidah 5:6 gives the acts of Wudu.

q: The second source of Islamic law is the:
e: The Sunnah explains and applies the Quran.

q: The six-member council to choose the third Caliph was appointed by:
e: Umar named six leading Companions before his death.

q: Who was sent as the first envoy and teacher of Islam to Madinah before the Hijrah?
e: He was sent after the First Pledge of Aqabah.

q: The first Ghazwa in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part was:
e: ). The expedition of Abwa took place in 2 AH without fighting.

q: Who was the commander of the Muslim army sent to Syria just before the Prophet's (PBUH) death?
e: Hazrat Abu Bakr kept Usama in command and dispatched the army.

q: Zakat was made obligatory in:
e: Zakat and fasting were both made obligatory in 2 AH.

q: The Nisab of silver for Zakat is:
e: 52.5 tolas of silver is about 612 grams.

q: Wearing two unstitched sheets and making the intention for Hajj or Umrah is called:
e: Ihram is put on at or before the Miqat.

q: The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa consists of how many rounds?
e: It starts at Safa and ends at Marwa.

q: Which prophet is called "Kalimullah" because Allah spoke to him directly?
e: ). An-Nisa 4:164 says Allah spoke directly to Musa.

q: Which prophet built the Ark at Allah's command?
e: ). Hazrat Nuh preached for 950 years.

q: Who rebuilt the Ka'bah with Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
e: ). Father and son raised its foundations (Al-Baqarah 2:127).

q: The first Qibla of the Muslims was:
e: Muslims faced Jerusalem until 2 AH.

q: Which Umayyad prince, called "the Falcon of the Quraysh", founded the Emirate of Cordoba in Spain?
e: Abdur Rahman ad-Dakhil founded the emirate in 756 CE.

q: Giving preference to a stronger legal reason over strict analogy in the public interest (a method used widely by Hanafis) is called:
e: Istihsan means juristic preference.

q: In Iqbal's thought, "Ijtihad" is described as:
o: A closed door after the four Imams
The principle of movement in the structure of Islam
e: He argues this in the sixth lecture of the Reconstruction.

q: Who conquered Sindh in 712 CE?
e: He defeated Raja Dahir; Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam.

q: Which ruler of Sindh was defeated by Muhammad bin Qasim?
e: Raja Dahir was killed in the battle near Rawar.

q: Who sent Muhammad bin Qasim to Sindh?
e: Hajjaj was governor of Iraq under the Umayyad Caliph Walid I.

q: How many times did Mahmud of Ghazni invade India?
e: His seventeen expeditions included the attack on Somnath in 1025–26.

q: Which scholar came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote "Kitab-ul-Hind"?
e: Al-Biruni studied Indian sciences and society.

q: Who won the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192?
e: Ghori had lost the first battle in 1191 and won the second.

q: Who founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206?
e: Aibak, a slave general of Ghori, founded the Slave dynasty.

q: Where is Qutbuddin Aibak buried?
e: He died in 1210 after a fall while playing polo in Lahore.

q: Who was the first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
e: Razia, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled from 1236 to 1240.

q: Which is the correct order of the Delhi Sultanate dynasties?
e: The Sultanate lasted from 1206 to 1526.

q: Which Sultan introduced market price controls?
e: He fixed prices to maintain a large army cheaply.

q: Which Sultan shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and issued token currency?
e: Both experiments failed.

q: Which traveller from Morocco visited India in the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
e: He served as a judge in Delhi.

q: Who invaded India and sacked Delhi in 1398?
e: Timur's invasion broke the Tughlaq state.

q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
e: Babur's victory founded the Mughal Empire.

q: The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between the forces of Akbar and:
e: Bairam Khan led Akbar's army.

q: Who defeated the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat (1761)?
e: Abdali's victory checked Maratha power.

q: "Tuzk-e-Babri", the memoir of Babur, was written in:
e: Babur wrote in Chagatai Turkish.

q: Who defeated Humayun and built the Grand Trunk Road?
e: He also built Rohtas Fort and introduced the silver rupee.

q: Who introduced "Din-e-Ilahi"?
e: Akbar introduced it in 1582; Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi opposed it.

q: "Ain-e-Akbari" was written by:
e: Abul Fazl also wrote the Akbarnama.

q: Which Mughal emperor is buried at Shahdara, Lahore?
e: Jahangir's tomb stands on the bank of the Ravi.

q: Who built the Shalimar Gardens of Lahore?
e: They were laid out in 1641–42.

q: Who built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore?
e: It was completed in 1673.

q: Who was the last Mughal emperor?
e: He was exiled to Rangoon after 1857.

q: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between Robert Clive and:
e: The betrayal of Mir Jafar decided the battle.

q: Tipu Sultan was martyred in 1799 at:
e: He fell in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

q: In which year did the British annex Sindh?
e: Sir Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Amirs at Miani.

q: In which year did the British annex the Punjab?
e: It followed the Second Anglo-Sikh War.

q: Who invited Ahmad Shah Abdali to India to check the Marathas?
e: Shah Waliullah (1703–1762) wrote to Abdali.

q: Syed Ahmad Shaheed was martyred in 1831 at:
e: He fell fighting the Sikhs with Shah Ismail Shaheed.

q: Who founded the Faraizi Movement in Bengal?
e: It called Muslims back to their religious duties (Faraiz).

q: The War of Independence of 1857 began at:
e: Soldiers rose at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

q: Which Act transferred the rule of India from the East India Company to the British Crown?
e: The Governor-General then became the Viceroy.

q: The East India Company was founded in:
e: It received a royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I.

q: Which Mughal emperor's court received Sir Thomas Roe as English ambassador?
e: Roe arrived in 1615.

q: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi, known as Mujaddid Alf Sani, opposed the religious policy of:
e: He rejected Din-e-Ilahi and wrote his famous letters.

q: The "Fatawa-e-Alamgiri", a digest of Islamic law, was compiled under:
e: Aurangzeb Alamgir ordered its compilation.

q: Which ruler of the Punjab died in 1839, after which Sikh power declined?
e: Ranjit Singh ruled from Lahore from 1799.

q: After the death of Aurangzeb in 1707, the Mughal Empire:
o: Was taken over by the Portuguese
e: Wars of succession and invasions weakened it.

q: Who founded the M.A.O. College at Aligarh?
e: The school opened in 1875 and became a college in 1877.

q: Which pamphlet did Sir Syed write on the causes of the 1857 uprising?
e: He blamed British policies and the lack of Indian representation.

q: In which year did Sir Syed start the journal "Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq"?
e: It aimed at the social reform of Muslims.

q: The Urdu-Hindi controversy began in 1867 at:
e: It convinced Sir Syed that Hindus and Muslims would go separate ways.

q: The Scientific Society was founded by Sir Syed in 1863 at:
e: It translated modern works into Urdu.

q: Who founded the Darul Uloom Deoband in 1866?
e: It became a leading seminary.

q: Nadwatul Ulama was established in 1894 at:
e: It tried to bridge the Aligarh and Deoband approaches.

q: Anjuman-e-Himayat-e-Islam was founded in 1884 in:
e: It ran schools, colleges and orphanages.

q: Who founded the Sindh Madressatul Islam in Karachi in 1885?
e: Quaid-e-Azam studied there.

q: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
e: Hume was a retired British civil servant; Bonnerjee was the first president.

q: Who partitioned Bengal in 1905?
e: It created a Muslim-majority province of East Bengal and Assam.

q: In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled?
e: The annulment was announced at the Delhi Durbar.

q: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906?
e: The deputation asked Lord Minto for separate electorates.

q: Where was the All-India Muslim League founded in December 1906?
e: It was founded at the annual meeting of the Muhammadan Educational Conference.

q: Who was the first president of the All-India Muslim League?
e: The Aga Khan was its first permanent president.

q: Separate electorates for Muslims were first granted by the:
e: The Indian Councils Act 1909 accepted the Simla Deputation's demand.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the Muslim League?
e: He had joined the Congress in 1906.

q: Under the Lucknow Pact of 1916, the Congress accepted:
e: It was the only time Congress and the League agreed on a joint scheme.

q: Who called Jinnah "the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity"?
e: The title came after his work for the Lucknow Pact.

q: The system of "dyarchy" in the provinces was introduced by the:
e: Provincial subjects were split into reserved and transferred lists.

q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in 1919 at:
e: General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering.

q: The Khilafat Movement was launched mainly to:
e: It was led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali.

q: The Simon Commission was boycotted in India mainly because:
o: It was headed by an Indian
e: All seven members were British.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was unacceptable to Muslims mainly because it:
e: Jinnah's amendments were rejected.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
e: They answered the Nehru Report.

q: Allama Iqbal delivered his famous Allahabad Address in:
e: He proposed a Muslim state in north-west India.

q: The Round Table Conferences (1930–1932) were held in:
e: Three conferences discussed India's future constitution.

q: Who announced the Communal Award of 1932?
e: It kept separate electorates and extended them to other minorities.

q: Who coined the name "Pakistan" in the pamphlet "Now or Never" (1933)?
e: He was then a student at Cambridge.

q: Which Act gave provincial autonomy and proposed an all-India federation?
e: Its federal part never came into force.

q: Sindh was separated from the Bombay Presidency in:
e: The separation took effect under the 1935 Act.

q: The Congress ministries (1937–1939) resigned in protest against:
o: India being taken into the Second World War without consultation
e: They resigned in late 1939.

q: The "Day of Deliverance" was observed by the Muslim League on:
e: Muslims marked the end of the Congress ministries.

q: The "Pirpur Report" documented:
o: The proceedings of the Simla Conference
Injustices against Muslims under the Congress ministries
e: It was issued in 1938.

q: The Lahore Resolution was passed on:
e: It was passed at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park.

q: Who moved the Lahore Resolution?
e: He was the premier of Bengal, known as Sher-e-Bangal.

q: The Cripps Mission came to India in:
e: It offered dominion status after the war.

q: The "Quit India" movement was launched by the Congress in:
e: The Muslim League stayed out of it.

q: The Simla Conference of 1945 failed mainly over:
o: The status of the princely states

q: "پانی پانی ہونا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: شرم سے پسینے پسینے ہو جانا۔

e: اچانک بری خبر سے سخت گھبرا جانا۔

q: "ٹس سے مس نہ ہونا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: کسی بات کا ذرا اثر نہ لینا۔

e: دشمن کو بری طرح ہرانا۔

q: "دال نہ گلنا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: کوشش کا کامیاب نہ ہونا۔

e: دھوکا دینے کے لیے خوش نما وعدے کرنا۔

e: "آج کل اسی کا طوطی بولتا ہے"۔

q: "قلعی کھلنا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟

q: "کان بھرنا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: چغلی کھا کر بدگمان کرنا۔

e: افسوس کرنا؛ مصافحے کے لیے "ہاتھ ملانا" آتا ہے۔

q: "آ بیل مجھے مار" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
e: جان بوجھ کر مشکل میں پڑنا۔

q: "ایک انار سو بیمار" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
o: چیز ایک اور چاہنے والے بہت
e: جب چیز کم ہو اور طلب گار زیادہ۔

q: "اونچی دکان پھیکا پکوان" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
o: نام بڑا مگر اصلیت کچھ نہیں
e: ظاہری شان کے مقابلے میں کم تر حقیقت۔

q: "ناچ نہ جانے آنگن ٹیڑھا" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
o: اپنی نااہلی کا الزام دوسروں پر رکھنا
e: کام نہ آئے تو بہانے بنانا۔

q: "دودھ کا جلا چھاچھ بھی پھونک پھونک کر پیتا ہے" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
o: ایک بار نقصان اٹھانے والا ہر بات میں احتیاط کرتا ہے
e: تلخ تجربہ انسان کو محتاط بنا دیتا ہے۔

q: "نیم حکیم خطرۂ جان" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
o: ادھورا علم نقصان دہ ہوتا ہے
e: اناڑی سے کام لینا خطرناک ہے۔

q: "چور کی داڑھی میں تنکا" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟

q: "جس کی لاٹھی اس کی بھینس" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
o: طاقت ور ہی کی چلتی ہے
e: زور والے کا حق مانا جاتا ہے۔

o: ایک مصیبت سے نکل کر دوسری میں پھنسنا
e: مشکل پوری طرح حل نہ ہونا۔

e: اسم، فعل اور حرف۔

q: وہ کلمہ جو کسی شخص، جگہ یا چیز کا نام ہو، کیا کہلاتا ہے؟

q: کسی خاص شخص، جگہ یا چیز کے نام کو کیا کہتے ہیں؟
e: مثلاً قائدِ اعظم، کراچی۔ عام نام اسمِ نکرہ ہے۔

q: "میں، تم، وہ" قواعد میں کیا ہیں؟
e: ضمیر وہ لفظ ہے جو اسم کی جگہ آئے۔

e: یہ قریب کے لیے اور وہ دور کے لیے۔

q: "وہ آیا تھا" کون سا زمانہ ہے؟
e: "تھا" ماضی بعید کی علامت ہے۔

q: "وہ آتا تھا" کون سا زمانہ ہے؟

q: "وہ آیا ہوگا" کون سا زمانہ ہے؟
e: اس میں شک یا گمان پایا جاتا ہے۔

q: "کاش وہ آتا" کون سا زمانہ ہے؟
e: اس میں تمنا یا شرط کے معنی ہوتے ہیں۔

q: "احمد سویا" میں "سویا" کون سا فعل ہے؟
e: فعلِ لازم صرف فاعل پر پورا ہو جاتا ہے۔

q: "اس نے خط لکھا" میں "لکھا" کون سا فعل ہے؟
e: فعلِ متعدی فاعل کے ساتھ مفعول بھی چاہتا ہے۔

q: "خط لکھا گیا" کون سا فعل ہے؟
e: فعلِ مجہول میں فاعل معلوم نہیں ہوتا۔

q: "پڑھ لیا، لکھ ڈالا، رو دیا" کس کی مثالیں ہیں؟
e: فعل). دو فعل مل کر ایک معنی دیتے ہیں؛ دوسرا امدادی فعل کہلاتا ہے۔

q: "جھوٹ مت بولو" کون سا فعل ہے؟
e: فعلِ نہی میں کسی کام سے روکا جاتا ہے۔

q: "احمد نیک ہے" کون سا جملہ ہے؟
e: اس میں مبتدا (احمد)، خبر (نیک) اور فعلِ ناقص (ہے) ہیں۔

section: درست جملہ اور الفاظ کی جوڑی
q: "نذر" اور "نظر" میں درست فرق کیا ہے؟
o: نذر: پیش کش یا منت؛ نظر: نگاہ
e: "کتاب آپ کی نذر ہے" اور "اس کی نظر تیز ہے"۔

q: "کسرت" اور "کثرت" میں درست فرق کیا ہے؟
e: "کسرت سے صحت بنتی ہے" اور "بارش کی کثرت"۔

section: درست جملہ اور الفاظ کی جوڑی
q: "نقطہ" اور "نکتہ" میں درست فرق کیا ہے؟
o: نقطہ: حرف پر لگنے والا نشان؛ نکتہ: باریک بات
e: "ب کے نیچے ایک نقطہ ہے" اور "اس نے اچھا نکتہ اٹھایا"۔

q: لفظ "اردو" کس زبان کا ہے اور اس کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: اردو ترکی لفظ ہے جس کے معنی لشکر یا چھاؤنی ہیں۔

q: آئینِ پاکستان کی کس دفعہ میں اردو کو قومی زبان قرار دیا گیا ہے؟
e: عدالتِ عظمیٰ نے 2015 میں اردو کو سرکاری زبان کے طور پر نافذ کرنے کا حکم دیا۔

q: "بابائے اردو" کسے کہا جاتا ہے؟
e: وہ انجمن ترقیِ اردو کے روحِ رواں تھے۔

q: "خدائے سخن" کس شاعر کو کہا جاتا ہے؟
e: میر کو غزل کا امام مانا جاتا ہے۔

q: "بانگِ درا" کس کی تصنیف ہے؟
e: اقبال کی دیگر اردو کتب: بالِ جبریل، ضربِ کلیم، ارمغانِ حجاز۔

q: "مسدسِ حالی" کا اصل نام کیا ہے؟
e: حالی کی دیگر کتب: مقدمۂ شعر و شاعری، یادگارِ غالب، حیاتِ جاوید۔

q: اردو کا پہلا ناول "مراۃ العروس" کس نے لکھا؟

q: "باغ و بہار" کس کی تصنیف ہے؟
e: یہ فورٹ ولیم کالج میں لکھی گئی؛ "فسانۂ عجائب" سرور کی ہے۔

q: مرثیہ نگاری میں سب سے مشہور نام کون سا ہے؟
e: میر انیس اور مرزا دبیر مرثیے کے بڑے شاعر ہیں۔

q: "آبِ حیات" کس کی تصنیف ہے؟
e: یہ اردو شعرا کا تذکرہ ہے۔

q: "He has been reading since morning." کا درست ترجمہ کیا ہے؟
o: وہ صبح سے پڑھ رہا ہے۔
e: Present perfect continuous کا ترجمہ "سے ... رہا ہے" سے ہوتا ہے۔

q: "If you had worked hard, you would have passed." کا درست ترجمہ کیا ہے؟

اگر تم محنت کرو تو کامیاب ہو سکتے ہو۔
اگر تم محنت کرو گے تو کامیاب ہو جاؤ گے۔
اگر تم محنت کرتے تو کامیاب ہو جاتے۔
e: یہ ماضی کی غیر حقیقی شرط ہے، اس لیے ماضی تمنائی آئے گا۔

q: "The work will have been finished by evening." کا درست ترجمہ کیا ہے؟
o: شام تک کام ختم ہو چکا ہوگا۔
شام تک کام ختم ہو رہا تھا۔
شام سے کام ختم ہو چکا ہے۔
e: Future perfect کا ترجمہ "چکا ہوگا" سے ہوتا ہے۔

q: "وہ جا چکا تھا۔" کا درست انگریزی ترجمہ کیا ہے؟
e: "چکا تھا" past perfect ہے۔

q: "مجھے یہاں رہتے ہوئے دس سال ہو گئے ہیں۔" کا درست انگریزی ترجمہ کیا ہے؟
o: I am living here since ten years.
I was living here for ten years.
I have been living here for ten years.
e: مدت کے ساتھ present perfect continuous اور "for" آتا ہے۔

q: How many Paras (Juz) does the Holy Quran have?
e: The Quran is divided into 30 Paras for monthly recitation.

q: In which month did the revelation of the Quran begin?
e: The Quran says it was sent down in Ramadan (2:185).

q: Which Surah is named after an insect that makes honey?
e: An-Nahl means the bee; An-Naml is the ant and Al-Ankabut the spider.

q: The second Surah of the Quran is:
e: Al-Fatihah is the first and Al-Baqarah the second.

q: The book of Hadith compiled by Imam Muslim is called:
e: It is the second of the six authentic books.

q: A Hadith whose chain stops at a Companion is called:
e: Marfu goes back to the Prophet (PBUH) himself.

q: Who was the grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
e: He looked after the Prophet until the age of eight.

q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to which clan of the Quraysh?
e: His mother Amina belonged to Banu Zuhrah.

q: Who went with the Holy Prophet (PBUH) on the Hijrah to Madinah?
e: Hazrat Ali stayed behind to return people's deposits.

q: The old name of Madinah was:
e: It was renamed Madinat-un-Nabi after the Hijrah.

q: The bond of brotherhood set up in Madinah between the Muhajirin and the Ansar is called:
e: Each emigrant was paired with a helper of Madinah.

q: In the Battle of Uhud, the Muslim archers were posted on:
e: Leaving this post exposed the army's rear.

q: Which prayer has three Fard Rak'ats?
e: Fajr has two and the others four.

q: On whom is Zakat obligatory?
o: A Muslim who owns the Nisab for one lunar year
e: Wealth must reach the Nisab and stay for a year.

q: The night spent in worship between 26 and 27 Rajab commemorates:
e: It is known as Shab-e-Mi'raj.

q: Which Caliph ordered the army of Usama to march despite the unrest in Arabia?
e: He refused to cancel an order given by the Prophet (PBUH).

q: During whose Caliphate was Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Maqdis) first taken by the Muslims?
e: Hazrat Umar travelled there to receive the city.

q: Islamic economics differs from both capitalism and socialism because it:
o: Permits private ownership but treats wealth as a trust with duties
Leaves the poor to the market
e: Zakat, inheritance and the ban on interest keep wealth moving.

q: When a new problem needs a legal ruling, the soundest approach is to:
o: Go back to the Quran and Sunnah and reason from their principles and aims
Leave the matter undecided for ever
e: This is the method of Ijtihad.

q: Tolerance in Islamic civilisation is best understood as:
o: Respecting others' right to their faith while holding to one's own
Treating all actions as equally right
Avoiding all contact with other faiths
e: "There is no compulsion in religion" (Al-Baqarah 256).

q: "حق" کی جمع کیا ہے؟
e: "حقائق" حقیقت کی جمع ہے۔

q: "مدرسہ" کی جمع کیا ہے؟
e: "دروس" درس کی جمع ہے۔

q: "عقیدہ" کی جمع کیا ہے؟
e: جیسے فریضہ سے فرائض۔

q: ان میں سے مذکر لفظ کون سا ہے؟
e: "اچھا خواب" درست ہے۔

q: "مور" کی مؤنث کیا ہے؟
e: مور سے مورنی۔

q: "خورشید" کا مترادف کیا ہے؟
e: خورشید، آفتاب اور مہر ہم معنی ہیں۔

q: "کوہ" کا مترادف کیا ہے؟
e: جیسے کوہِ ہمالیہ۔

q: "رفیق" کا مترادف کیا ہے؟
e: رفیق بمعنی دوست یا ساتھی۔

q: "بلندی" کا متضاد کیا ہے؟
e: بلندی و پستی۔

q: "فتح" کا متضاد کیا ہے؟
e: فتح جیت ہے اور شکست ہار۔

q: "حاضر" کا متضاد کیا ہے؟
e: حاضر و غائب۔

q: "آنکھوں کا تارا ہونا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: بہت عزیز شخص کے لیے بولا جاتا ہے۔

q: "اینٹ سے اینٹ بجانا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: کسی جگہ کو بالکل اجاڑ دینا۔

q: "چراغ پا ہونا" کے معنی کیا ہیں؟
e: غصے سے بھڑک اٹھنا۔

q: "جیسا دیس ویسا بھیس" کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
o: جہاں رہو وہاں کے طور طریقے اپناؤ
ہر ملک کا لباس الگ ہے
e: ماحول کے مطابق چلنا چاہیے۔

q: "لکھنا، پڑھنا، دوڑنا" قواعد میں کیا کہلاتے ہیں؟
e: مصدر کے آخر میں "نا" آتا ہے۔

q: "وہ خط لکھ رہا ہے" کون سا زمانہ ہے؟
e: کام اس وقت جاری ہے۔

q: "اے، او، ارے" کیا کہلاتے ہیں؟
e: یہ پکارنے کے لیے آتے ہیں۔

q: درست جملہ کون سا ہے؟
o: آج شب کی برات رات ہے۔
آج شبِ برات کا رات ہے۔
آج شبِ برات کی رات ہے۔
e: "شب" کے معنی ہی رات ہیں۔

q: "I have been waiting for you for two hours." کا درست ترجمہ کیا ہے؟
o: میں دو گھنٹے بعد تمھارا انتظار کرتا ہوں۔
میں نے دو گھنٹے تمھارا انتظار کیا تھا۔
میں دو گھنٹے تمھارا انتظار کروں گا۔
میں دو گھنٹے سے تمھارا انتظار کر رہا ہوں۔
e: Present perfect continuous کا ترجمہ "سے ... رہا ہوں" سے ہوتا ہے۔

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ARDUOUS.
e: Arduous means needing great effort.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CONCISE.
e: Concise writing says much in few words.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to DOCILE.
e: A docile animal is easy to control.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ERUDITE.
e: An erudite person has great knowledge.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to FUTILE.
e: A futile effort produces no result.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to IMPECCABLE.
e: Impeccable means without any fault.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to REBARBATIVE.
e: Rebarbative means unattractive and off-putting.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to SAGACIOUS.
e: Sagacious means showing good judgement.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to AFFLUENT.
e: Affluent means wealthy.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to COMPLACENT.
e: Complacent means smugly satisfied.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to DIFFIDENT.
e: Diffident means lacking self-confidence.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to INDOLENT.
e: Indolent means lazy.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to PRECARIOUS.
e: Precarious means unsafe or uncertain.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to RETICENT.
e: A reticent person says little.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to SUPERFLUOUS.
e: Superfluous means more than is needed.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Either the teacher or the students was to blame.
Either the teacher or the students are to blame.
Either the teacher or the students has to blame.
Either the teacher or the students is to blame.
e: With "either ... or" the verb agrees with the nearer subject.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The quality of these mangoes are good.
The quality of these mango are good.
The qualities of this mangoes is good.
The quality of these mangoes is good.
e: The subject is "quality", which is singular.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Being rainy day, we stayed home.
It being a rainy day, we stayed at home.
Being a rainy day, we stayed at home.
Being a rainy day, home was where we stayed.
e: The phrase needs its own subject "it"; otherwise it wrongly describes "we".

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Not only he is intelligent but also hard-working.
He is not only intelligent but also hard-working.
He not only is intelligent but also hard-working.
He is not only intelligent but also works hard.
e: "Not only ... but also" must join two similar forms.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Scarcely the bell had rung when the students ran out.
Scarcely had the bell rung than the students ran out.
Scarcely had the bell rung when the students ran out.
Scarcely had the bell rang when the students ran out.
e: "Scarcely" takes inversion and "when".

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I look forward to meet you.
I am look forward to meeting you.
I look forward to meeting you.
e: "Look forward to" is followed by the "-ing" form.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He denied having taken the money.
He denied to take the money.
He denied that he takes the money.
He denied to have took the money.
e: "Deny" is followed by a gerund.

q: Fill in the blank: If it ______ tomorrow, we shall cancel the trip.
e: In a first conditional the "if" clause takes the present tense.

q: Fill in the blank: She has been absent ______ Monday.
e: "Since" is used with a point of time.

q: Fill in the blank: The thief ______ before the police arrived.
e: The earlier past action takes the past perfect.

q: Fill in the blank: He was accused ______ cheating in the test.
e: "Accused of".

q: Fill in the blank: This rule is applicable ______ all members.
e: "Applicable to".

q: Fill in the blank: She is engaged ______ a banker.
e: A person is engaged to another person.

q: Fill in the blank: He is engaged ______ writing a report.
e: A person is engaged in an activity.

q: Fill in the blank: I differ ______ you on this point.
e: To "differ with" a person is to disagree; things "differ from" each other.

q: "To add fuel to the fire" means:
o: To make a bad situation worse
e: It worsens anger or trouble.

q: "A bone of contention" is:
e: It is the matter people fight over.

q: "To turn over a new leaf" means:
o: To change one's ways for the better
e: The person makes a fresh start.

q: "To pay through the nose" means:
e: The price paid is excessive.

q: "To take the bull by the horns" means:
o: To take a risk for fun
e: The person deals with the problem directly.

q: The witness gave a ______ account that convinced the court.
e: "Credible" means believable.

q: He was ______ from the charge after the new evidence came in.
e: "Exonerated" means cleared of blame.

q: The minister made an ______ to Iqbal's poetry in his speech.
e: An "allusion" is an indirect reference.

q: The two reports ______ each other, so one of them must be wrong.
e: "Contradict" means to state the opposite.

q: His ______ manner made him popular with everyone.
e: "Affable" means friendly and easy to talk to.

q: Carpenter : Saw :: Tailor : ______
e: Each worker is paired with a tool.

q: Drop : Ocean :: Grain : ______
e: A drop is a tiny part of an ocean as a grain is of a desert.

q: Cold : Freezing :: Warm : ______
e: The second word is an extreme degree of the first.

q: A person who looks on the dark side of things is:
e: A pessimist expects the worst.

q: A place where coins are made is:
e: Coins are struck in a mint.

q: According to the passage, most bridges fail because of:
e: "Far more decay slowly."

q: The phrase "empties the budget" means that slow decay:
o: Is very costly in the end
Is paid for by the news media
e: Late repairs cost far more than early ones.

q: In the passage, "those who hold the purse" are:
e: They decide what money is spent on.

q: The author's main recommendation is to:
o: Keep up regular inspection and small repairs
e: Early sealing prevents very expensive repairs.

q: Inspection is cut first, according to the passage, because:
o: A standing bridge appears to need nothing
It is more costly than rebuilding
e: The last sentence gives this reason.

q: Simplify: 11 + 9 × 7 − 45 ÷ 5
e: Multiply and divide first: 9 × 7 = 63 and 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Then 11 + 63 − 9 = 65.

q: If 27^k = 9, what is the value of k?
e: Write both sides as powers of 3: 3^(3k) = 3^2. So 3k = 2 and k = 2/3.

q: A man spends 1/4 of his salary on rent and 1/6 on food. He is left with Rs 21,000. What is his salary?
e: Fraction left = 1 − 1/4 − 1/6 = 7/12. So 7/12 of the salary = 21,000, and the salary = 21,000 ÷ 7/12 = Rs 36,000.

q: A price is increased by 50% and the new price is then reduced by 50%. What is the net change?
e: Multiply the factors: 1.5 × 0.5 = 0.75. Net change: 25% decrease.

q: A's salary is 300% more than B's. By what percentage is B's salary less than A's?
e: Let B = 100, so A = 400. B is less by 300 out of 400, which is 75%.

q: A student needs 33% marks to pass. He gets 139 marks and fails by 26 marks. What are the maximum marks?
e: Pass marks = 139 + 26 = 165. This is 33% of the maximum, so maximum = 165 × 100 ÷ 33 = 500.

q: After a discount of 25%, an article is sold for Rs 4,200. What is its marked price?
e: Selling price is 75% of the marked price. Marked price = 4,200 × 100 ÷ 75 = Rs 5,600.

q: Two successive discounts of 20% and 20% are equal to a single discount of:
e: Single discount = a + b − ab/100 = 20 + 20 − 4 = 36%.

q: Rs 2,500 is lent at 5% simple interest per year. What amount is due after 2 years?
Rs 33,600 is divided among three people in the ratio 2 : 4 : 6. What is the smallest share?
e: Total parts = 12. One part = 33,600 ÷ 12 = 2,800. The smallest share = 2 × 2,800 = Rs 5,600.

q: A 48-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 3?
e: Milk = 36 litres, water = 12 litres. Milk stays the same, so water must become 36 litres. Add 36 − 12 = 24 litres.

q: If A : B = 5 : 6 and B : C = 3 : 4, what is A : B : C?
e: Make B the same in both ratios (LCM of 6 and 3 is 6). The combined ratio is 5 : 6 : 8.

q: In a class, 20 boys have an average score of 49 and 30 girls have an average score of 59. What is the average score of the whole class?
e: Total = 20 × 49 + 30 × 59 = 2750. Divide by 50 students: 55. The simple mean of 49 and 59 is wrong because the groups are unequal.

q: The arithmetic mean of 16, 14, 22, 16 and x is 25. What is the value of x?
e: Total must be 5 × 25 = 125. The four known numbers add up to 68. So x = 125 − 68 = 57.

q: The ages of two brothers are in the ratio 7 : 5 and add up to 48 years. How old will the elder brother be after 2 years?
e: One part = 48 ÷ 12 = 4. The elder is 7 × 4 = 28 now and will be 30 after 2 years.

q: For what value of x is 4(x − 3) + 2 = 1x + 35?
e: Expand: 4x − 12 + 2 = 1x + 35. So 3x = 45 and x = 15.

q: What are the roots of x² + 3x − 4 = 0?
e: The roots must add up to −3 and multiply to −4. The numbers −4 and 1 do both.

q: The sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 63. What is the largest of them?
e: The middle number is 63 ÷ 3 = 21. The three numbers are 19, 21, 23, so the largest is 23.

q: x² + 16x − 4 is written in the form (x + a)² + b. What is the value of b?
e: Half of 16 is 8, so (x + 8)² = x² + 16x + 64. Then b = −4 − 64 = −68.

q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular polygon with 18 sides?
e: Sum of interior angles = (18 − 2) × 180° = 2880°. Each angle = 2880 ÷ 18 = 160°.

q: The area of a circle is 154 cm². What is its radius? (Take π = 22/7.)
A ladder 41 m long leans against a wall with its foot 9 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
e: Height² = 41² − 9² = 1600, so the height is 40 m.

q: Each side of a square is decreased by 50%. By what percentage does its area change?
e: Area factor = (0.5)² = 0.25. The area decreases by 75%.

q: 12 men can finish a piece of work in 6 days. How long will 6 men take to finish the same work?
e: Work = 12 × 6 = 72 man-days. Time for 6 men = 72 ÷ 6 = 12 days. More men, fewer days.

q: A tap can fill a tank in 10 hours and a drain can empty the full tank in 15 hours. If both are open, how long will it take to fill the empty tank?
e: Net filling in one hour = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30. Time = 30 hours.

q: A train 150 m long runs at 45 km/h. How long does it take to pass a platform 250 m long?
A car covers 112 km in 1 hours 45 minutes at a steady speed. What is its speed?
e: Time = 7/4 hours. Speed = 112 ÷ 7/4 = 64 km/h.

q: A thief is 1,200 m ahead of a policeman. The thief runs at 8 km/h and the policeman at 12 km/h. How long does the policeman take to catch him?
e: The gap closes at 12 − 8 = 4 km/h. Time = 1.2 km ÷ 4 km/h = 3/10 hour = 18 minutes.

q: In a group of 60 people, 32 like tea, 21 like coffee and 14 like both. How many like neither?
e: At least one = 32 + 21 − 14 = 39. Neither = 60 − 39 = 21.

q: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the two numbers add up to 10?
e: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. The favourable ones are (4,6), (5,5), (6,4): 3 in all. Probability = 1/12.

q: At a meeting, each of 8 people shakes hands once with every other person. How many handshakes take place?
e: Each pair shakes hands once: n(n − 1) ÷ 2 = 8 × 7 ÷ 2 = 28.

q: What is the next number in the series 1, 3, 9, 27, 81, 243, ...?
e: Each term is 3 times the previous term. The next term is 729.

q: What is the next number in the series 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, 216, ...?
e: The terms are cubes of 1, 2, 3 ... . The next term is 343.

q: What is the next number in the series 6, 39, 10, 34, 14, 29, ...?
e: Two series alternate: one rises by 4, the other falls by 5. The next term is 18.

q: What comes next in the series ABE, BCF, CDG, DEH, ...?
e: Each letter moves one place forward in every term. The next term is EFI.

q: What comes next in the series BDF, CEG, DFH, EGI, ...?
e: Each letter moves one place forward in every term. The next term is FHJ.

q: A sequence starts with 9. To get each next term you alternately multiply by 2 and subtract 3, starting with the multiplication. What is the 7th term?
e: The terms are 9, 18, 15, 30, 27, 54, 51. The 7th term is 51.
In the first pair the second number is the square of the first. Apply the same rule to 5: 25.

q: In a certain code, PLANT is written as SODQW. How is BRICK written in that code?
e: Each letter is moved 3 places forward in the alphabet. So BRICK becomes EULFN.

q: In a code, letters are numbered backwards (Z = 1, Y = 2, ... A = 26) and WAX is written as 4-26-3. How is OWL written?
e: Each letter becomes 27 minus its normal position. OWL is 12-4-15.

q: A man walks 8 km north, then 12 km east, then 3 km south. How far is he from his starting point?
e: His net movement is 5 km north and 12 km east. Distance = √(5² + 12²) = 13 km.

q: A man is facing south. He turns 90° to his right, then 135° to his right, and then 180° to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
e: Count right turns as clockwise and left turns as anticlockwise from south. He ends up facing south-west.

q: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 2:30?
e: Hour hand: 30 × 2 + 0.5 × 30 = 75°. Minute hand: 6 × 30 = 180°. The smaller angle between them is 105°.

q: A clock shows 2:10. What time does its image in a mirror appear to show?
e: Subtract the time from 12:00 (think of 11:60). 11:60 − 2:10 = 9:50.

q: Today is Saturday. What day of the week will it be 500 days from today?
e: 500 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 3. Count 3 day(s) forward from Saturday: Tuesday.

q: 1 January 2027 is a Friday. What day of the week is 20 December 2027?
e: 2027 is not a leap year. From 1 January to 20 December is 353 days, and 353 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 3. Count 3 day(s) forward from Friday: Monday.

q: A bus leaves a stop every 52 minutes. A clerk says: "The last bus left 39 minutes ago and the next one leaves at 10:50." At what time is the clerk speaking?
e: The last bus left at 10:50 minus 52 minutes = 9:58. Add 39 minutes: 10:37.

q: In a class of 56 students, Omar ranks 15th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
e: Rank from the bottom = 56 − 15 + 1 = 42.

q: Ghani is taller than Ejaz. Ejaz is taller than Danish. Imran is taller than Ghani. Danish is taller than Junaid. Who is the second tallest?
e: Putting the clues together, the order from tallest to shortest is Imran, Ghani, Ejaz, Danish, Junaid. So the answer is Ghani.

q: Ghani is shorter than Ejaz. Junaid is shorter than Bilal. Bilal is shorter than Fahad. Ghani is taller than Fahad. Who is the shortest?
e: Putting the clues together, the order from tallest to shortest is Ejaz, Ghani, Fahad, Bilal, Junaid. So the answer is Junaid.

q: If the words Contain, Contact, Contest, Context are arranged as in a dictionary, which word comes second?
e: Dictionary order: Contact, Contain, Contest, Context. The second word is Contain.

q: Pointing to a boy, Hina said, 'He is the son of my mother's only child.' How is the boy related to Hina?
e: Her mother's only child is Hina herself. So the boy is her son.

q: Some trainers are assessors. All assessors are certified. Which conclusion must be true?
e: The trainers who are assessors are certified, so some trainers are certified.

q: All cats are mammals. Some mammals are kept as pets. Which statement is definitely true?
o: No cat is kept as a pet
Some cats are kept as pets
e: All cats are mammals, so some mammals are cats. The statements do not say whether the pet mammals include cats.

q: What is the negation of 'Some shops are open'?
e: To deny "some are" you must say "none is".

q: Which statement is the contrapositive of 'If a number is divisible by 6, it is divisible by 3'?
o: If a number is not divisible by 3, it is not divisible by 6
A number divisible by 3 is never divisible by 6
If a number is divisible by 3, it is divisible by 6
If a number is not divisible by 6, it is not divisible by 3
e: Swap and negate both parts: "not Q → not P".

q: Five houses in a row are numbered 1 to 5 from west to east. The doctor lives in house 3. The teacher lives east of the doctor but not at the end. The clerk lives next to the teacher, on the east side. Who lives in house 5?
e: The teacher must be in house 4, so the clerk is in house 5.

q: Which is the odd one out: square, rectangle, rhombus, triangle?
e: A triangle has three sides; the others have four.

q: Which pair is the odd one out: (2, 4), (3, 9), (5, 25), (6, 30)?
e: ). In the other pairs the second number is the square of the first.

q: How old is Ali? Statement I: Ali is twice as old as Bilal. Statement II: Bilal is 5 years younger than Chand.
o: Even both statements together are not sufficient
e: No actual age is given anywhere, so the ages cannot be found.

q: Which instrument measures temperature?
e: Clinical thermometers measure body temperature.

q: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
e: One coulomb is one ampere flowing for one second.

q: In an election between two candidates, the winner got 62% of the valid votes and won by 4,080 votes. How many valid votes were cast?
e: The loser got 38%. The margin is 62% − 38% = 24% of the votes = 4,080. Total = 4,080 × 100 ÷ 24 = 17,000.

q: A student needs 50% marks to pass. He gets 193 marks and fails by 7 marks. What are the maximum marks?
e: Pass marks = 193 + 7 = 200. This is 50% of the maximum, so maximum = 200 × 100 ÷ 50 = 400.

q: After a discount of 20%, an article is sold for Rs 5,600. What is its marked price?
e: Selling price is 80% of the marked price. Marked price = 5,600 × 100 ÷ 80 = Rs 7,000.

q: Two successive discounts of 25% and 40% are equal to a single discount of:
e: Single discount = a + b − ab/100 = 25 + 40 − 10 = 55%.

Rs 46,200 is divided among three people in the ratio 6 : 7 : 8. What is the largest share?
e: Total parts = 21. One part = 46,200 ÷ 21 = 2,200. The largest share = 8 × 2,200 = Rs 17,600.

q: A 75-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 4 : 2?
e: Milk = 60 litres, water = 15 litres. Milk stays the same, so water must become 30 litres. Add 30 − 15 = 15 litres.

q: The average of 6 numbers is 53. When one more number is included, the average becomes 54. What is the new number?
e: Old total = 6 × 53 = 318. New total = 7 × 54 = 378. New number = 378 − 318 = 60.

q: A car travels from A to B at 20 km/h and returns over the same road at 30 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
e: For equal distances, average speed = 2uv ÷ (u + v) = 2 × 20 × 30 ÷ 50 = 24 km/h. It is not the simple mean 25.

q: The average weight of 8 people rises by 2 kg when one of them, who weighs 40 kg, is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
e: The total rises by 8 × 2 = 16 kg. New person = 40 + 16 = 56 kg.

q: The ages of two brothers are in the ratio 3 : 2 and add up to 20 years. How old will the elder brother be after 7 years?
e: One part = 20 ÷ 5 = 4. The elder is 3 × 4 = 12 now and will be 19 after 7 years.

q: For what value of x is 6(x − 1) + 12 = 3x + 45?
e: Expand: 6x − 6 + 12 = 3x + 45. So 3x = 39 and x = 13.

q: What are the roots of x² − 12x + 35 = 0?
e: The roots must add up to 12 and multiply to 35. The numbers 5 and 7 do both.

q: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 78. What is the largest of them?
e: The middle number is 78 ÷ 3 = 26. The three numbers are 24, 26, 28, so the largest is 28.

q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 4 : 5. What is the largest angle?
e: The angles add up to 180°. One part = 180 ÷ 10 = 18°. Largest = 5 × 18 = 90°.

q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular polygon with 12 sides?
e: Sum of interior angles = (12 − 2) × 180° = 1800°. Each angle = 1800 ÷ 12 = 150°.

q: A rectangular water tank is 4 m long, 1.5 m wide and 75 cm deep. How many litres of water can it hold?
e: Volume = 4 × 1.5 × 0.75 = 4.5 m³. One cubic metre is 1,000 litres, so the tank holds 4,500 litres.

q: A ladder 13 m long leans against a wall with its foot 5 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
e: Height² = 13² − 5² = 144, so the height is 12 m.

q: Each side of a square is increased by 50%. By what percentage does its area change?
e: Area factor = (1.5)² = 2.25. The area increases by 125%.

q: 24 men can finish a piece of work in 20 days. How long will 40 men take to finish the same work?
e: Work = 24 × 20 = 480 man-days. Time for 40 men = 480 ÷ 40 = 12 days. More men, fewer days.

q: One pipe fills a tank in 30 hours and another fills it in 45 hours. How long do they take together?

q: A train 125 m long runs at 45 km/h. How long does it take to pass a platform 200 m long?
A boat travels at 22 km/h downstream and 16 km/h upstream. What is its speed in still water?

q: In a 200 m race, Ali finishes in 20 seconds and Babar in 25 seconds, each at a steady speed. By what distance does Ali beat Babar?

q: A bag holds 8 red, 2 green and 5 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is either red or green?

q: What is the median of 23, 35, 13, 6, 5, 20, 34?

q: 8 teams play a knockout tournament in which the loser of each match is eliminated. How many matches are needed to find the champion?

q: What is the next number in the series 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, 126, ...?

q: What is the next number in the series 3, 9, 27, 81, 243, 729, ...?

q: In a certain code, BREAD is written as ZPCYB. How is CLOUD written in that code?

q: In a code, letters are numbered backwards (Z = 1, Y = 2, ... A = 26) and CAT is written as 24-26-7. How is INK written?

q: A man walks 5 km south and then 12 km west. How far is he from his starting point?
e: The two legs are at right angles. Distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.

q: A man is facing west. He turns 180° to his right, then 135° to his left, and then 180° to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
e: Count right turns as clockwise and left turns as anticlockwise from west. He ends up facing south-east.

q: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 2:10?

q: A clock shows 8:35. What time does its image in a mirror appear to show?

q: Today is Friday. What day of the week will it be 75 days from today?
e: 75 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 5. Count 5 day(s) forward from Friday: Wednesday.

q: 1 January 2030 is a Tuesday. What day of the week is 15 March 2030?
e: 2030 is not a leap year. From 1 January to 15 March is 73 days, and 73 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 3. Count 3 day(s) forward from Tuesday: Friday.

q: A bus leaves a stop every 50 minutes. A clerk says: "The last bus left 32 minutes ago and the next one leaves at 9:00." At what time is the clerk speaking?
e: The last bus left at 9:00 minus 50 minutes = 8:10. Add 32 minutes: 8:42.

q: In a class of 57 students, Omar ranks 11th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?

q: Bilal is lighter than Chand. Chand is lighter than Junaid. Ghani is lighter than Asad. Asad is lighter than Bilal. Who is exactly in the middle?

q: If the words Infant, Inform, Infer, Inflate are arranged as in a dictionary, which word comes last?

q: A is the brother of B. B is the sister of C. C is the father of D. How is A related to D?

q: The HCF of two numbers is 15 and their LCM is 90. If one number is 30, what is the other?
